cards.text: Paul just told the elders of the church in Ephesus they'd never see his face again, and they all wept. Now Paul and his travel crew tear themselves away and sail to Cos, then Rhodes, then Patara. Destination: Jerusalem, where the Holy Spirit has warned him, town after town, that chains and afflictions are waiting.

cards.question: At Patara, Paul's crew finds a ship crossing over to a new region. Where's it headed?

cards.text: They spot Cyprus, pass south of it and land at Tyre in Syria. And friend, that ship isn't stopping because Paul asked nicely.

cards.question: So why does the ship stop at Tyre?

cards.text: They look up the disciples in Tyre and stay SEVEN DAYS. That's not a layover, friend, that's moving in.

cards.question: Through the Spirit, the disciples in Tyre keep telling Paul not to go up to ___.
After all those warnings in Tyre, Paul calls off the trip and stays there.

cards.text: When the week's up, the whole church walks them out of the city, wives and kids too. That's not a goodbye, friend. That's a PARADE.

cards.question: Down on the beach outside Tyre, what does everyone do before Paul's crew leaves?

answers.text: Read a letter from Ephesus together

cards.text: Goodbyes said, Paul's crew boards the ship and the folks from Tyre head home. The voyage ends at Ptolemais, where they greet the brothers.

cards.question: Paul's crew stays with the brothers in Ptolemais for ___.

cards.text: The next day they reach Caesarea and stay at the home of Philip the evangelist, one of the Seven chosen to serve the church back in Acts 6:5. Tyre got a week, Ptolemais got one day, and now Philip's guest room is about to get BUSY.

cards.question: Philip has four unmarried daughters who prophesy.

cards.text: Several days in, a prophet named Agabus comes down from Judea. He's the same Agabus who predicted a great famine back in Acts 11:28.
Agabus walks over, takes a belt and ties up his own feet and hands with it. No hello, no small talk, friend, just a grown man tying himself up in the middle of the visit.

cards.question: Agabus ties up his own hands and feet with a belt. Whose belt is it?
Agabus says the Holy Spirit says the Jews of Jerusalem will bind the owner of this belt and hand him over to the ___.

cards.text: Paul's crew and the people of Caesarea hear it, and they ALL plead with Paul not to go up to Jerusalem. Me? I'd have wrapped my mustache around his ankle and held on.

cards.question: Paul answers the people pleading with him. For the name of the Lord Jesus, what does he say he's ready for in Jerusalem?

answers.text: To be bound and even to die
To argue his case in court
To preach and then slip away

cards.question: Paul tells the people pleading with him that their weeping is breaking his heart.
Paul won't be talked out of going, so his friends quiet down. What do they say?

cards.text: After these days, they pack up and go on to Jerusalem. Every stop warned him, friend, and Paul still packs like he's got FRONT-ROW TICKETS.

cards.question: Who goes along with Paul's crew on the way to Jerusalem?

cards.text: Those disciples take them to stay at the home of Mnason the Cypriot, an early disciple. Warned in Tyre, warned in Caesarea, and Paul keeps right on going, friend.

rule.text: He calls the baker "baker" or "friend," and talks to one baker at a time. Never "my baker," "kids" or "sweetie."

findings.problem: The opening card uses facts from the previous passage without references. These are the Ephesian elders never seeing Paul's face again and all weeping (Acts 20:25, 37-38), Jerusalem as Paul's destination (Acts 20:22) and the Holy Spirit's warnings of chains and afflictions (Acts 20:23). The card cites only Acts 21:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Paul first appears here, but the card never says who he is.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Card 1 already says "Destination: Jerusalem" and that the warnings are about what waits there. That gives away the blank in card 6 ("not to go up to ___"). Either reword card 1 or ask card 6 about something else in Acts 21:4.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: "The next day they reach Caesarea" adds an arrival time. Acts 21:8 says only that they left the next day ("Leaving the next day, we went on to Caesarea"). It does not say when they arrived.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: "He's the same Agabus who predicted a great famine back in Acts 11:28" states that the two are the same man. Neither Acts 11:28 nor Acts 21:10 says so. Acts 21:10 simply introduces "a prophet named Agabus."

rule.text: Connecting passages. When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: "Every stop warned him" is presented as a fact, but it isn't true in this passage. No warning comes at Cos, Rhodes, Patara or Ptolemais. Only Tyre (21:4) and Caesarea (21:11-12) warn him.

rule.text: What he points out must be true.
